title: Sheinbaum Supervises Construction of the Mexico City-Querétaro Passenger Train; “It’s Progressing According to Schedule”
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez
Jiménez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez,%20Enviado)
originally appeared in the [October 31, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/31/politica/sheinbaum-
supervisa-trabajos-de-construccion-del-tren-de-pasajeros-cdmxqueretaro-va-
avanzando-conforme-al-programa), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Polotitlán, State of Mexico**. With **32 percent progress** and 90 percent
of the right-of-way cleared, construction of the Mexico City-Querétaro
passenger train "is progressing according to schedule," President Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo stated this Saturday, specifying that the project is part of
nearly 2,500 kilometers of railways to be built during the six-year term, with
an investment of **around 700 billion pesos**.

While supervising the work at kilometer 137, the president toured about 13
kilometers of the route, accompanied by the governors of the State of Mexico,
Delfina Gómez, and of Hidalgo, Julio Menchaca; General Gustavo Vallejo, head
of the general construction residency, and Andrés Lajous, head of the Railway
Transport Regulatory Agency (ARTF), as well as cabinet officials.

Sheinbaum highlighted that the train "is faster" than cars, since on these
routes "there is very heavy saturation on the highways," and that the Mexico
City-Querétaro route "is solving a mobility problem for what is the central
zone of the country, really a very large metropolitan area." She added that in
some areas it will operate "like an urban train" and that its construction
generates jobs and regional development.

General Vallejo reported that the project "is 32 percent complete," with 12
construction fronts in operation, and that the front visited registers almost
39 percent. He detailed that there are currently **around 18,500 active jobs**
and that the train will cover the route in about two hours, with speeds of up
to 180 kilometers per hour on some stretches.

For his part, Lajous explained that the route, of around 230 kilometers from
Buenavista to downtown Querétaro, will be double-track, with diesel-electric
trains. He indicated that 47 trainsets are already contracted and being
manufactured in Ciudad Sahagún, Hidalgo, and that all stations will connect
with local public transportation.
